# The Problem

Applying statistical classification methods—and Discriminant Analysis in particular—in R currently requires users to identify, coordinate, and execute dozens of independent, function-based packages across multiple analytical stages. To execute a methodologically sound analysis, users must write custom command-line scripts to connect specialized libraries for missing value handling (`imputeTS`), multivariate normality and covariance testing (`MVN`, `CovCorTest`), multicollinearity and model diagnostics (`car`, `performance`), tree-based modeling and ROC evaluation (`partykit`, `pROC`), and custom visualization (`ggplot2`, `ggparty`). This fragmented, syntax-heavy workflow creates a steep technical barrier that directly impacts applied researchers, university students, educators, and domain analysts who require robust statistical modeling but lack advanced R coding expertise, often leading them to omit critical preliminary diagnostic checks and compromise statistical rigor.

While existing function-based packages provide powerful individual algorithms, they lack a consolidated, guided workflow that seamlessly connects data preparation and assumption diagnostics to model fitting and automated interpretation within a single environment. To address this limitation, the proposed project unifies these disjointed tools into a single, standardized R package. By enabling users to simply install the library and launch a transparent, interactive GUI via a single command (e.g., `run_app()`), the package eliminates the coding requirement while preserving full statistical rigor and transparency across the entire analytical workflow.
